Good context drop. The haptic research I just did strengthens several points in that synthesis. Key updates:
The GELLO force extension numbers are now concrete: 62%→93% on drawer opening, and the implementation uses DYNAMIXEL current control to reflect external torque estimates—no additional F/T sensors needed. That's your sub-$500 bilateral system right there. DexForce's 76% vs 0% result is the strongest argument for why your motion capture suit needs force feedback, not just position tracking. Position-only demonstrations literally cannot teach dexterous tasks like unscrewing nuts or opening AirPods cases. The force information isn't optional. The Bi-ACT architecture validates your hierarchy: it predicts joint angles, velocities, AND forces. Including force in both observations and action targets outperforms force-in-observation-only. Your motor group policies should output force targets, not just position targets, even if the low-level controller converts them to current commands. What's new that matters for your stack:
Sensorless force estimation via disturbance observers enables bilateral control at the STM32 level without wrist F/T sensors. ROBOTIS OpenMANIPULATOR-X does this at 1kHz using accurate dynamics models. Your hybrid neural-PID joint controllers could estimate external force as a byproduct of the neural feedforward—same computation, free force feedback. CMU's FACTR system achieved 64.7% improvement using "force-attending curriculum training"—start with easy force-insensitive tasks, gradually introduce contact-rich tasks.
